item.title: Pope Leo calls for dialogue over conflict, says young Catholics are a sign of hope
item.summary: # Pope Leo calls for dialogue over conflict, says young Catholics are a sign of hope - Click here to listen to this article - Share via - During visits to San Marino and Rimini, Pope Leo XIV delivers his strongest appeal yet for dialogue over war and polarization, urging Christians to heal a world fractured by conflict and fear. - In tiny San Marino, the American pope praises a republic built on freedom and mutual respect, calling it a ‘laboratory of good politics’ that defends human dignity. - At Rimini’s Catholic festival, Leo urges believers to confront unjust economic and technological systems, asserting that ‘there can be no enemies’ and hailing young Catholics as a hopeful antidote to despair. SAN MARINO — Pope Leo XIV used a visit to the tiny landlocked nation of San Marino and a major Catholic gathering in the Italian city of Rimini on Saturday to issue one of his strongest appeals yet against war, polarization and social division, urging believers to foster dialogue and friendship in a fractured world.
